prf:knot-operator-selection:
Proof Proof of knot operator selection. Sketch.

(i) The Hecke algebra H_r(q) is semisimple for generic q, so \mathrm{End}_{H_r(q)}(V^{\otimes r}) decomposes as \bigoplus_\lambda \mathrm{End}(V_\lambda) by the Wedderburn theorem. The Markov trace projects onto each component with weight d_\lambda(q) by Schur orthogonality (RJ inner product).

(ii) The categorical action \mathfrak{S} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes \Phi) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A = \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) is linear in \Phi. Substituting the spectral decomposition (i) and using the identification \mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{tr}_M (archimedean descent) gives the stated sum over channels.

(iii) The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_F = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\hat\beta_a) \cdot \rho(\hat\beta_b)) is the categorical inner product. Non-degeneracy (QUO-1) means every element has a unique Frobenius dual. In the NF basis, this identifies positive coefficients with morphisms \mathbf{1} \to A (supply, via coevaluation) and negative coefficients with morphisms A \to \mathbf{1} (demand, via evaluation).

(iv) The on-shell condition constrains \Phi to lie in the self-dual curvature subspace (S([\sigma_i, \sigma_j])^* = [\sigma_i, \sigma_j]). Within this subspace, the extremum of |\mathrm{tr}(\Phi)| is attained at the irrep with largest quantum dimension times character evaluation. For pair production at the observed q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps), this is T_{2,3} (trefoil, e^-) — the lowest-crossing operator that unconditionally opens the degree-3 channel.

Explicit dual construction

Consider a state K \in H_3(q) with decomposition K = \sum_i c_i b_i. The Frobenius dual K^\vee is the unique element satisfying

  \langle K^\vee, b_i \rangle_F = c_i
  \quad \forall i.

By non-degeneracy (read on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate; on H_n itself \det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical), K^\vee exists and is unique. In the basis, K^\vee = \sum_i c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j, where G_{ij} = \langle b_i, b_j \rangle_F = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) is the 6 \times 6 Gram matrix of H_3(q).

The demand vector of K is the negative part:

  \mathrm{dem}(K) = \sum_{i : c_i < 0} |c_i| \, b_i^\vee.

The operator that fills the demand at minimum crossing energy is

  \Phi_{\mathrm{min}}
  =
  \arg\min_{\Phi \in \mathrm{End}(A)_{\mathrm{on-shell}}}
  \left\{
    \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\Phi)
    \ \Big|\ 
    \langle \Phi, \mathrm{dem}(K) \rangle_F \geq
    \|\mathrm{dem}(K)\|_F
  \right\}.

For the positron (e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1}), the demand profile is \{-0.218\gamma, -0.209 L_+, -0.209 L_-\}. The positron word demands vacuum energy and L_\pm content. The minimum-energy supply is the coevaluation \mathrm{coev}_A \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee, which provides exactly the identity and Hopf content from the rigid structure. Its cost is \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A) = [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \approx 2.011.
rem:knot-operator-selection-multichannel:
Remark Multi-channel interpretation of knot operator selection. The Lagrangian endomorphism \Phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) of the categorical action decomposes over the irreducible representations of H_n(q). This decomposition and the Frobenius self-duality A \cong A^\vee determine the specific knot operators that mediate any interaction and their corresponding weights.

Multi-channel interpretation

For Breit--Wheeler pair production \gamma\gamma \to e^-e^+, the full interaction is

  \mathcal{S}(\gamma_1, \gamma_2)
  =
  \underbrace{d_{\mathrm{triv}}(q) \cdot P_{T_{1,0}}}_{\text{elastic: polarisation change}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\Box}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,1}}}_{\text{single crossing}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\Box\Box}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,2}}}_{\text{Hopf link (gluon)}}
  +
  \underbrace{d_{\yng(2,1)}(q) \cdot P_{T_{2,3}}}_{\text{trefoil}}
  +  \cdots

All channels fire simultaneously. Two incoming photons can:

  • change polarisation (trivial operator, no pair created),
  • exchange a gluon (T_{2,2}, Hopf link),
  • pass through the trefoil operator T_{2,3}; under the electron ruling (electron) the e^-e^+ pair is read from the \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 coefficient (Breit--Wheeler pair production), not from this channel,
  • pass through the cinquefoil operator T_{2,5}, suppressed by higher crossing energy; the muon word is not ruled, so this is not yet a \mu^-\mu^+ channel.

These events occur in a single interaction. The quantum dimension d_\lambda(q) weights each channel. The branching ratios depend entirely on q and the incoming photon polarisation content \varphi_0, \varphi_1.

Experiments detect the dominant channel, which carries the largest weight. The subdominant channels contribute to radiative corrections, vacuum polarisation, and the running of coupling constants. The elastic channel (T_{1,0}) is always present: photon--photon scattering without pair creation is the leading process, and pair creation is a threshold-activated subdominant channel.
prose:intro-mesons-nucleons:
Once quark–antiquark pairs are generated at a Hecke vertex, colour confinement restricts observable states to closed links whose total colour holonomy is trivial. The simplest composite state is a meson, formed by a quark strand and an antiquark strand joined into a two-component link along a single colour tube.

Forming a baryon requires three quark strands. Rather than linking pairwise, the three strands close into the Borromean rings \mathcal{B}_3—a Brunnian link in which every two-component sublink is trivial yet the three-component closure is topologically inseparable. This section defines the meson formation chain and proves the existence of the categorical proton as the minimal-action Borromean closure bounded by the hadronic scale \mathfrak{E}_0.
rem:meson-formation-chain:
Remark The meson formation chain. The meson arises through a three-step formation chain.

Step 1: Pair production. A 1.6\% energy gap separates the bare photon pair from the threshold 2\mathfrak{m}_e. The color weights \varphi_0, \varphi_1 close this gap by supplying Hopf link terms. Two colored photons \gamma_i = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} thus fuse into an electron--positron pair:

  \gamma_1 \cdot \gamma_2
   \longrightarrow 
  e^- + e^+
  +  \text{\(L_\pm\) content}(L_+ = \varphi_0\psi_1, L_- = \varphi_1\psi_0)

Step 2: Quark creation. To create a quark on the e^- channel, L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 from the colored photon normal form acts as a creation operator:

  L_+ \cdot e^-
  = 
  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0)
  \xrightarrow{\mathrm{NF}}
  \mathfrak{u} + \varphi_0\psi_1\cdot e^-

Two independent pair productions create two quark--antiquark channels: \mathfrak{u} + \bar{\mathfrak{u}} and \mathfrak{d} + \bar{\mathfrak{d}}.

Step 3: Meson binding. To form the meson, a quark from one production binds with an antiquark from the other. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H mediates this binding:

  \mathfrak{u} + \bar{\mathfrak{d}}
  \xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}_H}
  \mathfrak{M}_+
  = 
  T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{10}

Summary chain.

  \gamma\gamma
  \xrightarrow{\text{Breit--Wheeler}}
  e^- e^+
  \xrightarrow{L_+}
  q\bar{q}
  \xrightarrow{\mathcal{L}_H}
  \mathfrak{M}

Each arrow is a morphism in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q). Breit--Wheeler multiplies by \sigma_0^2. Quark creation left-multiplies by L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1. Meson binding inserts \mathcal{L}_H = \sigma_0\sigma_1 between the quark and antiquark crossing pairs. Evaluating at q = q_0 yields the meson normal form:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_+)
  = 
  +0.209\sigma_1
  +  1.044 L_+
  +  0.044 L_-
  +  0.218 e^-

This produces the net value \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) = +1.515.

prop:categorical-proton-exists:
Proposition Existence of the categorical proton. The categorical proton exists as a well-defined element of the Hecke algebra H_3(q):

\mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) \in H_3(q).

It satisfies Frobenius stability G x[\gamma] \ge 0 at every step of the LP reduction.

Archimedean specialisation. The underlying categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. Their archimedean realisation requires real- or complex-analytic constructs. What follows invokes these constructs—real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. What follows therefore sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.
prf:categorical-proton-exists: Proof Proof of existence of the categorical proton. The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0 \sigma_1^{-1})^3 is a concrete element of the braid group B_3, and thus of the Hecke algebra H_3(q) via the standard representation. Typed crossings for the partition (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) and the gluon stabiliser L_- = \sigma_1 \sigma_0 are likewise elements of H_3(q). Their product reduces via Gröbner--Shirshov to a canonical Hecke normal form. LP-dual feasibility verifies the non-negativity constraint G x[\gamma] \ge 0 at every intermediate step. Consequently, the categorical proton \mathfrak{p} exists as a well-defined, LP-stable element.
sec:mesons-nucleons-categorical-proton-u: Within the three-strand Borromean link topology, the orientation of the internal trefoil twist distinguishes the two nucleon isospin states. This section proves the uniqueness of the categorical proton and categorical neutron in H_3(q), constructs the meson-to-proton Borromean lifting morphism, and demonstrates that crossing reversal \sigma_i \leftrightarrow \sigma_i^{-1} maps particles to antiparticles while exchanging left- and right-handed trefoil chirality between the electron and positron.
prop:categorical-proton-unique:
Proposition Uniqueness of the categorical proton up to braid isotopy. The triple (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) and the Borromean braiding pattern \mathcal{B}_3 uniquely determine the categorical proton \mathfrak{p} up to braid isotopy:

\mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) \in H_3(q).

Its Hecke normal form in H_3(q) is unique, and the S_3 permutation symmetry on the color tubes ensures independence from position assignments.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. The categorical identities hold over an abstract coefficient ring. Only the archimedean realization requires specialization.
prf:categorical-proton-unique: Proof Proof of uniqueness of the categorical proton. The argument inherits from the uniqueness of hadrons. The Hecke normal form is unique in H_3(q). Permuting the colour tubes (r, g, b) acts via inner Hecke automorphisms that fix the normal-form class, establishing the S_3-symmetry. Specifically, the three position assignments (\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d}), (\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{u}), and (\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u}) produce Hecke elements related by S_3-conjugation. They therefore reduce to the same normal form. Among feasible stabilisers, minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M| uniquely selects the LP-optimal gluon choice (L_- = \sigma_1 \sigma_0).
rem:meson-to-proton-via-borromean:
Remark Proton formation: three pair productions and the energy scale \mathbf{E}_0. Baryon number conservation prevents adding a quark to a meson to form a proton. A meson consists of a quark--antiquark pair (q\bar{q}) and carries baryon number B = 0. A single quark carries B = 1/3. Their sum q\bar{q} + q yields B = 1/3. A baryon requires B = 1. Baryon number conservation prevents the antiquark from spontaneously converting into a quark.

Meson instability at q_0

The meson lacks stability at q_0. The normal form of the \mathfrak{u}\bar{\mathfrak{d}} meson (\sigma_0 \cdot L_+ \cdot \sigma_0^{-1}) in H_3(q) is:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_+)
  =
  -0.209\sigma_1 - 0.044 L_+ + 1.000 L_- + 0.209 e^-

This yields \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx +0.956 and demand profile \{\sigma_1 = -0.209, L_+ = -0.044\}. Two negative normal form coefficients demand crossing content (\sigma_1) and L_+ content from the environment.

This demand renders the meson a transient intermediate rather than a stable endpoint. Observations align with this property. The charged pion decays in \sim 26 ns. Borromean topology \mathcal{B}_3 confinement provides genuine 3-body binding. This produces the only stable hadronic states, the proton and neutron.

Three pair productions yield one proton

The proton requires three quarks (\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) with no antiquarks. Three independent quark--antiquark productions supply these constituents. Colliding colored photons create each q\bar{q} pair:

  \gamma\gamma \xrightarrow{L_+}
  \mathfrak{u}_1 + \bar{\mathfrak{u}}_1
  \qquad
  \gamma\gamma \xrightarrow{L_+}
  \mathfrak{u}_2 + \bar{\mathfrak{u}}_2
  \qquad
  \gamma\gamma \xrightarrow{L_-}
  \mathfrak{d}_3 + \bar{\mathfrak{d}}_3

The Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 confines three quarks (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2, \mathfrak{d}_3) selected from these six particles:

  \mathfrak{p}
  = 
  \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d})

The three antiquarks (\bar{\mathfrak{u}}_1, \bar{\mathfrak{u}}_2, \bar{\mathfrak{d}}_3) annihilate back to photons or form an antiproton \bar{\mathfrak{p}}. Total baryon number remains conserved: 3 \times (1/3 - 1/3) = 0 input, 1 + (-1) = 0 output.

Typed crossings: the physical proton and neutron

Untyped composition yields \mathrm{net} \approx 1.506. The CODATA proton net is \approx 0.999. Typed crossings close this gap. Quark flavor determines the crossing eigenvalue in H_3(q).

Crossing type Hecke eigenvalue
\mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{u} (\sigma) +q
\mathfrak{d}-\mathfrak{d} (\sigma - h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}) -q^{-1}
\mathfrak{u}-\mathfrak{d} (\sigma - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1}) mixed

The term h_{\mathrm{A}} equals q - q^{-1}. Down-quark crossings carry a -h_{\mathrm{A}}\cdot\mathbf{1} shift. This shift reduces the net coefficient.

Typed crossings at q_0 \approx 1.1100 produce:

Nucleon Quark content \mathrm{net}
Proton \mathfrak{p} \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d} +0.9991
Neutron \mathfrak{n} \mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d} +0.8108

The scale \mathfrak{E}_0 = Q / |\Delta\mathrm{net}|

The normal form coefficients represent dimensionless Laurent polynomials in q. Converting them to physical energies (MeV) requires a single scale \mathfrak{E}_0. The beta decay Q-value fixes this scale.

  1. Linearity. The normal form computation constitutes a linear map on the 6-dimensional vector space H_3(q). Therefore, \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{n} - \mathfrak{p}) = \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{n}) - \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{p}). The net difference equals the sum of all coefficient differences:

      \Delta\mathrm{net}
  = 
  \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) - \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{p})
  = 
  0.8108 - 0.9991
  = 
  -0.1883.

  2. Calibration. Beta decay \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar\nu_e releases \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} - \mathfrak{m}_e \approx 0.782 \text{ MeV}. This supplies the energy equivalent of the dimensionless transition \Delta\mathrm{net}:

      \mathfrak{E}_0
  = 
  \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta}{|\Delta\mathrm{net}|}
  = 
  \frac{0.782}{0.1883}
   \approx  4.155 \text{ MeV}.

  3. Well-definedness. The fixed aether parameter q_0 determines all normal form coefficients. CODATA 2022 measures \mathfrak{Q}_\beta to \pm 0.6 eV precision. Typed crossings mandate the negative sign \Delta\mathrm{net} < 0. The extra down quark in [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}] introduces -h_{\mathrm{A}} shifts. These shifts lower the neutron net below the proton net. The ratio remains well-defined.

The parameter \mathfrak{E}_0 dictates the energy budget. Each normal form coefficient difference \Delta_i contributes \Delta_i \times \mathfrak{E}_0 MeV to the decay energy. The six terms sum exactly to \mathfrak{Q}_\beta.

Full derivation. Minimum action principles derive the confinement operator \mathcal{B}_3. Nucleon normal forms remain independent of photon polarization. The beta decay channel emerges as the e^- < 0 coefficient in the confined normal form.

prop:antiparticle-crossing-reversal:
Proposition Antiparticles from crossing reversal. The electron is the word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron). Its mirror image, the positron e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (positron), has all crossings reversed.

Statement.

  1. Crossing reversal defines antiparticles. Replacing every constituent K_i with its mirror K_i^{\sigma} yields the antihadron \mathfrak{H}^{\sigma} of a composite hadron \mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}. The braid word \beta representing the linking has all crossing signs reversed.

  2. Crossing energy sign reversal. The crossing energy of \mathfrak{H} is

      \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = \sum_{\text{crossings}} \epsilon_i,
  \qquad \epsilon_i \in \{q, -q^{-1}\}.

    The crossing energy of the antihadron satisfies

      \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = -\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \bigg|_{q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}}.

    Positive crossings (+q) become negative (-q^{-1}) and vice versa.

  3. Coulomb charge reversal. The antisymmetric component of the crossing energy determines the Coulomb channel. This reverses sign: Q(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = -Q(\mathfrak{H}). The antiproton specifically carries Q(\mathfrak{p}^{\sigma}) = -1.

  4. Topological mass invariance. The mirror operation preserves the knot type and its hyperbolic volume. The topological mass of a particle equals that of its antiparticle: m_{\mathrm{topological}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = m_{\mathrm{topological}}(\mathfrak{H}).
rem:chirality-trefoil-electron-positron:
Remark Electron and positron words: a mirror pair. The electron is the word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron) and the positron is its mirror e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (positron), the same word with every crossing reversed. The mirror word is the inverse braid, e^+ = (e^-)^{-1}. The chirality assignment is conventional. The physical content resides in their mirror relationship.

Where the chirality lives. The closures are the positive and negative Hopf links. Unlike the trefoil (the backup electron, which is chiral as an unoriented knot), the Hopf link is amphichiral as an unoriented link: its mirror image is itself with one component reversed. So the electron and positron cannot be told apart by the unoriented link type of their closures. They are told apart by the braid itself and by the orientation of the closure. The writhe, a well-defined invariant of the braid, is +3 for e^- and -3 for e^+, so e^- \neq e^+ in B_3. The linking number of the oriented closure is +1 for e^- and -1 for e^+.

Antiparticles from crossing reversal.

Antihadron construction reverses every crossing in the knot formula, \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. Mirroring yields the antiproton:

  \mathfrak{p}^{\sigma}
  = 
  [u^{\sigma}, u^{\sigma}, d^{\sigma}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H

Each quark is an unknot strand carrying one crossing letter: \sigma_i for u and \sigma_i^{-1} for d. Mirroring reverses the letter, so u^{\sigma} carries \sigma_i^{-1} and d^{\sigma} carries \sigma_i. The crossing energy of \mathfrak{p}^{\sigma} reverses sign. This yields Coulomb charge Q(\mathfrak{p}^{\sigma}) = -1.

Time reversal and the exceptional divisor.

Traversing the exceptional divisor of the brane tower reverses every crossing of the electron word. This maps e^- to e^+ = (e^-)^{-1}. The Feynman--Stueckelberg interpretation maps this to a particle traveling backward in time. The fiber adjoint involution acts on the weight decomposition and reverses the Reeb flow. Extending this involution to the exceptional divisor provides a mechanism for chirality reversal. The vortex tube reverses winding orientation passing through the blow-up.

Open questions.

  1. Vortex inversion: Reversing circulation of a vortex tube in the brane fluid requires translating classical fluid dynamics results on vortex reconnection to the categorical setting.

  2. Information transfer: Double chirality reversal (electron \to positron \to electron) constitutes a round-trip through the time-reversed sector. The fiber adjoint involution satisfies \sigma^2 = \mathrm{id}. This returns the system to its original state. Information preservation across this round-trip depends on the exceptional divisor's monodromy.

  3. The imaginary part: The Archimedean realization over \mathbb{C} permits a complex aether parameter q. The observability axiom restricts q to positive reals. A nonzero imaginary part contributes a phase to the crossing energy. This phase distinguishes particles from antiparticles without mirror reflection. The full theory models chirality reversal as a continuous rotation rather than a discrete flip.

  4. CPT from the categorical algebra: The fiber adjoint involution and the Frobenius structure derive the combined CPT operation (charge conjugation \sigma, parity reflection, Reeb flow reversal). The QOU involutive axiom implies the CPT theorem.
prose:intro-stable-nucleus-torus-knots:
For a multi-nucleon braid closure to resist spontaneous topological fission, its colour-tube trajectory on the Reeb bundle \mathcal{R}_p \to \mathcal{S}_p must wind compatibly with the Hopf fibration. Links whose components fiber compatibly over the torus are the torus knots and links T(p, q), whose Seifert-fibered complements carry zero hyperbolic volume and therefore avoid hyperbolic volume tension.

This section defines the stable-nucleus locus, proves that torus–Hopf factorisation obstructs topological decay across the prime-power family T(p^n, q^n), establishes the left-projector chiral structure of the weak vertex, and proves the genus-4 uniqueness theorem: on Bring's surface, the Hurwitz genus bound and S_5 equivariance admit exactly two primitive torus-knot force carriers, T_{2,9} and T_{3,5}.
def:stable-nucleus:
Definition Stable nucleus (Skein energy minimum). Let \mathfrak{p} and \mathfrak{n} be the categorical proton and neutron (categorical proton, categorical neutron). The nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons (Z the atomic number) is the iterated Hopf link

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  = 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{p} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{p}}_{Z}
   \oplus 
  \underbrace{\mathfrak{n} \oplus \cdots \oplus \mathfrak{n}}_{N}.

The nucleus \mathcal{N}(Z, N) is stable if (Z, N) is a critical point of the Skein binding Lagrangian \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} (Skein binding Lagrangian) under beta variation (exchange of \mathfrak{p} \leftrightarrow \mathfrak{n} at fixed A = Z + N):

  \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}}{\partial Z}
  \bigg|_{A}
  = 0 .

A stable atom appends Z electrons e^- (electron):

  \mathcal{A}(Z, N)
  = 
  \mathcal{N}(Z, N)  \oplus  Z \cdot e^-,

rem:stable-nucleus-valley:
Remark The stability condition restricts the hadron to the valley of stability. Restricting the hadron definition. The abstract hadron (hadron) permits arbitrary multi-component composites. The stability condition restricts the physically realised nuclei to the valley of stability. Only configurations (Z, N) satisfying the beta-stability equation of the stable nucleus (beta-stability) are long-lived. Nuclei outside this valley undergo beta decay (\mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e or \mathfrak{p} \to \mathfrak{n} + e^+ + \nu_e) until they reach the stable configuration.

This is not an additional axiom. It is a strict consequence of the Skein binding Lagrangian. The parameter q determines both the strong binding (via (q + q^{-1})/2) and the Coulomb repulsion (via (q - q^{-1})/2). Their balance selects the unique stable (Z, N) for each mass number A.

Closed form of the critical point. The summary reading of the stable nucleus is a multi-nucleon Hopf link that extremizes the Skein binding Lagrangian. By beta-stability, its criticality condition is equivalent to

  Z = \frac{A}{2 + a_C  A^{2/3} / (2a_A)},

where a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C and a_A is the Pauli coefficient. The letter Z is the standard nuclear-physics notation for the proton count, which frees p for use as a brane point.
prop:torus-hopf-stability:
Proposition Torus knot composites on Bring's surface are stable hadrons. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6. Every baryon formed from torus knot generators \mathcal{G} linked by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H satisfies the stability condition

and is therefore a hadron.
prf:torus-hopf-stability:
Proof Proof of torus hopf stability. The torus knot generators T_{m,n} \in \mathcal{G} have meridional winding m \in \{2, 3\}, forced by the genus-4 bound. For any triple [K_1, K_2, K_3]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H drawn from \mathcal{G}:

  1. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H contributes a negative baseline crossing energy via the strong binding term \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q + q^{-1}).
  2. The Coulomb correction Q(\mathfrak{H}) \cdot (q - q^{-1}) satisfies |Q(\mathfrak{H})| \leq 1 for all generators in \mathcal{G}, because the genus constraint bounds the maximum crossing asymmetry between m = 2 and m = 3 strands.
  3. Since \tanh(\ln q) \approx 0.104, the Coulomb correction is at most \sim 10\% of the strong baseline, insufficient to overcome binding.

In particular:

  • Proton \mathfrak{p} = [T_{2,3}, T_{2,3}, T_{2,3}^{\sigma}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H: The Coulomb charge is Q(\mathfrak{p}) = +1. The positive Coulomb correction reduces binding but does not overcome it, leaving \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0.
  • Neutron \mathfrak{n} = [T_{2,3}, T_{2,3}^{\sigma}, T_{2,3}^{\sigma}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_H: The Coulomb charge is Q(\mathfrak{n}) = 0. The strong baseline binding is undiminished.

Both are stable hadrons. \square
rem:torus-knot-prime-powers:
Remark Prime-power structure of T_{3,p^k} generators. The torus knots T_{3,n} with n = p^k (prime power, p \neq 3) form subfamilies with exponentially growing genus. The Bring surface genus bound permits few of these.

Genus formula. For T_{3,p^k} with \gcd(3, p^k) = 1:

  g(T_{3,p^k}) = \frac{(3-1)(p^k - 1)}{2} = p^k - 1.

Embeddability requires p^k - 1 \leq 4, which implies p^k \leq 5.

The p = 2 tower: T_{3, 2^k}.

k Knot Genus = 2^k - 1 Crossings Embeddable? Assignment
1 T_{3,2} = T_{2,3} (trefoil 3_1) 1 3 Yes Backup electron e^- (the ruled electron \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 closes to the Hopf link)

The trefoil as self-intersection.

The identity T_{3,2} = T_{2,3} places the trefoil in both winding families simultaneously:

  T_{2,3} \in \{T_{2,n}\}_{n \text{ odd}} \qquad\text{and}\qquad T_{3,2} \in \{T_{3,p^k}\}_{p \neq 3}.

The p = 7 tower and beyond.

For p \geq 7, g(T_{3,p}) = p - 1 \geq 6 > 4. No knot T_{3,p^k} with p \geq 7 embeds.

Classification of embeddable T_{3,p^k}.

Matter vs. force dichotomy.

The power tower T_{3,2^k} establishes a physical pattern:

  • k = 2: T_{3,4}. Hopf{}^2 color binding (H^{0,1} force carrier).

The knot T_{3,5} is structurally distinguished from both matter generations. Its prime winding (n = 5, not a power of 2) and saturating genus (4) separate it from any power tower. This supports its force carrier interpretation.

Remark on T_{2,9}. The three-fold cover T_{2,9} has n = 9 = 3^2, a prime power in the m = 2 family. Its genus is (9 - 1)/2 = 4 (saturating).

rem:force-knot-identification:
Remark Force carriers from the involutive structure and saturating generators. The three Standard Model forces arise from three distinct layers of the torus knot architecture on Bring's surface. The saturating genus-4 generators T_{2,9} and T_{3,5} carry the strong and weak forces. Electromagnetism is not a knot. It is the involutive structure of the category itself.

I. Electromagnetism. Electromagnetism requires no dedicated torus knot generator. It exists in the \dagger-structure on \mathbf{C} and the crossing-sign decomposition of the Skein algebra.

The crossing energy at each site decomposes into symmetric and antisymmetric channels:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = 
  \underbrace{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}_{\text{mass (strong)}}
  + 
  \underbrace{E_{\mathrm{anti}}}_{\text{Coulomb (EM)}}.

The antisymmetric Coulomb channel reverses sign under the crossing reversal involution \sigma \colon K \mapsto K^{\sigma}. This implements charge conjugation C categorically. Electromagnetic charge is the eigenvalue of the involution \sigma acting on the crossing energy:

  Q(K) =  \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K)
  - \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(K^{\sigma})\bigr).

This involution descends from three interlocking structures on Bring's surface:

  1. The \dagger-involution on \mathbf{C}. The positive-definite contravariant endofunctor f \mapsto f^{\dagger} defines observability. Every morphism carries a sign under \dagger. The electromagnetic coupling is the component of the Skein pairing that is odd under this involution.
  2. The complex structure on the color elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_z. The embedding \Sigma_4 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^4 induces a Kähler structure on Bring's surface. The complex structure J satisfies J^2 = -1 and determines the phase of the crossing energy. Electromagnetic charge is the winding number of this phase around the \mathrm{U}(1) fiber of the Hopf map \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1.
  3. The symplectic pairing on the color tube coordinates. The T-duality involution \iota \colon (X, z) \mapsto (z, X) on the symmetric cubic F(X, z) = F(z, X) exchanges color and spacetime degrees of freedom. The symplectic form \omega = dX \wedge dz is invariant under \iota. The Coulomb interaction is the component of the crossing energy that transforms as a (1,1)-form under the complex structure.

Electromagnetism is intrinsic to any knot. Every charged particle (knot with nonzero antisymmetric crossing energy) automatically couples electromagnetically. This structure yields three consequences:

  • Universality. All charged particles interact, regardless of knot type or genus.
  • Charge quantisation. Q is an eigenvalue of an involution, hence discrete (\pm 1 for leptons, \pm 1/3, \pm 2/3 for quarks in the Borromean decomposition).
  • Masslessness. Electromagnetism is not carried by a knot. The \dagger-involution has no Seifert genus, contributing zero topological mass.

II. Strong force. The knot T_{2,9}, the three-fold cover of the trefoil, carries the strong interaction.

Property Value Physical implication
Winding 9 = 3 \times 3 Interpolates 3 color copies of T_{2,3}
Genus 4 (saturating) Maximal topological complexity
Crossings 9 (all same sign) Three crossing triples, one per color tube
Hyperbolic volume 0 Massless carrier (gluon)
Meridional strands m = 2 Same winding family as leptons/quarks

The strong force binds by interpolation. The knot T_{2,9} wraps through all three color fibers in a single closed curve. This provides the topological rigidity that confines quarks into baryons. The three S_3 subgroups of the automorphism group S_5 of Bring's surface are the subgroups that leave one of the three T_{2,3} periods of T_{2,9} invariant.

This topology forces confinement. The knot T_{2,9} cannot continuously deform to separate the three color copies without breaking the torus embedding. Extracting a single color strand requires cutting T_{2,9} into an open arc. This is topologically forbidden.

At scales smaller than the color tube radius, the three strands of T_{2,9} are locally parallel. The binding from their global winding vanishes. This yields asymptotic freedom.

III. Weak force. The knot T_{3,5} carries the weak interaction. It is the cross-family generator connecting m = 2 (leptons) and m = 3 (quarks).

Property Value Physical implication
Winding (3, 5) Bridges m = 3 (quark) and n = 5 (second generation)
Genus 4 (saturating) Near-boundary of embeddability
Crossings 10 High complexity \to weak coupling
Hyperbolic volume 0 Zero topological mass from volume; mass from crossings
Knot group \langle x, y \mid x^3 = y^5 \rangle Intertwines 3-color and 5-fold winding

The torus knot T_{3,5} uniquely combines winding numbers from both families: m = 3 from the quark sector, and n = 5 from the T_{2,5} column. This cross-link drives flavor-changing processes. The weak interaction transmutes quarks between generations and converts quarks to leptons because T_{3,5} topologically connects both sectors.

Parity violation follows from the Skein asymmetry at q \neq 1. In the Hecke algebra H_n(q) a positive crossing is the generator \sigma_i = L_+, a negative crossing is \sigma_i^{-1} = L_-, and the smoothing is 1 = L_0. The Skein relation is the Hecke relation multiplied by \sigma_i^{-1}:

  L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0 .

Weighting the two crossings unequally separates the two eigenlines of \sigma_i. Let P_+ and P_- be the idempotents of \sigma_i for its eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}; these are the left and right circular channels of the Breit–Wheeler vertex. With [2]_q = q + q^{-1},

  q\,\sigma_i - q^{-1}\sigma_i^{-1} = (q - q^{-1})\,[2]_q\,P_+ .

The q-weighted crossing difference therefore acts on one eigenline only, and it vanishes at q = 1. Let W_L = P_+\sigma_i^{-1}P_+ + P_-\sigma_i P_- be the element that inverts \sigma_i on the P_+ line and leaves the P_- line unchanged. It is the generator minus this difference:

  [2]_q\,W_L = [2]_q\,\sigma_i - \bigl(q\,\sigma_i - q^{-1}\sigma_i^{-1}\bigr).

Both identities hold for every q with q \neq 0 and q + q^{-1} \neq 0. Which eigenline is singled out is fixed by which crossing carries the weight q: the mirror weighting q^{-1}\sigma_i - q\,\sigma_i^{-1} gives (q - q^{-1})\,[2]_q\,P_- instead. This one-sidedness holds at a single crossing. The Markov trace of T_{3,5} at z = q^3/(q^2+1) is not supported on the left line.

The following is a model statement without derivation. The weak force maximizes this asymmetry because T_{3,5} has the highest crossing count (10) among generators, and the q-vs-q^{-1} imbalance accumulates over these crossings. No computation here relates the crossing count to the size of the asymmetry.

Unlike the massless T_{2,9}, T_{3,5} gives nonzero mass to the weak bosons. Its hyperbolic volume is zero, but its 10 crossings generate crossing energy via the mass formula. The 10 crossings of T_{3,5} do not cancel. This yields the massive W and Z. This too is a model statement without derivation: the crossing energy of T_{3,5} is not computed here, and no W or Z mass is derived from it.

Summary.

Force Source Knot? Mass Parity

Strong T_{2,9}: three-fold cover of trefoil Genus 4, vol = 0 Massless (color-averaged crossings cancel) Conserved

The genus-4 constraint \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 specifies all three forces.
prop:weak-vertex-left-projector:
Proposition The weak vertex insertion is proportional to the left projector. Let \sigma be a generator of H_n(q), so that \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1 with h = q - q^{-1}, and assume q \neq 0 and [2]_q = q + q^{-1} \neq 0. The generator has two eigenlines: the line on which it acts by q, with projector P_+ = (\sigma + q^{-1})/[2]_q, and the line on which it acts by -q^{-1}, with projector P_- = (q - \sigma)/[2]_q.

The left line P_L is the eigenline on which \sigma acts with an eigenvalue of modulus greater than 1, and the right line P_R = 1 - P_L is the other one. For |q| > 1 this gives P_L = P_+. The weak vertex W is the element that acts as \sigma^{-1} on the left line and as \sigma on the right line:

W \;=\; \sigma^{-1} P_L + \sigma\, P_R .

The difference between the weak vertex and the free crossing is a multiple of the left projector:

W - \sigma \;=\; -(q - q^{-1})\, P_L .

This holds for |q| > 1 and for |q| \leq 1. Three consequences follow.

  1. The difference W - \sigma annihilates the right line, and it acts on the left line by the scalar -(q - q^{-1}). It vanishes exactly when q - q^{-1} = 0.
  2. An element a + b\,\sigma annihilates the right line if and only if it is a scalar multiple of P_L. Within the algebra generated by one crossing, "the right line does not couple" and "proportional to P_L" are the same statement.
  3. Let t be the eigenvalue of \sigma of modulus greater than 1, whichever of q and -q^{-1} that is, and weight the positive crossing by it. Then the weighted crossing difference is
t\,\sigma - t^{-1}\sigma^{-1} \;=\; (t - t^{-1})(t + t^{-1})\, P_L .

So the choice of which crossing carries the weight, left open in the force-carrier identification, is the same choice as the left line.

Scope at the level of a knot. The statement is about one crossing. It does not extend to the trace of the weak knot T_{3,5}, the closure of (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5 in H_3(q). Under the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the part of that trace on the right line of \sigma_1 is

\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\, P_R\bigr) \;=\; -\frac{q^2}{(q^2+1)^3} \;\neq\; 0 .

At the proton-anchored q_0 this is -9.33\,\% of \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\bigr). All of it comes from the two-dimensional block of H_3(q), since y_{(1^3)} = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1). For the torus words (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^N the right-line part repeats with period 3 in N and is never zero.

This holds for every trace with y_{(2,1)} \neq 0, not only at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Write a trace on H_3(q) as \tau = y_{(3)}\chi_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}\chi_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\chi_{(1^3)}. Assume |q| > 1, so that P_R = P_-, and [3]_q \neq 0. Then \tau(x P_R) = 0 for every x if and only if y_{(2,1)} = y_{(1^3)} = 0. With \tau(1) = 1, such a trace is the augmentation \sigma_i \mapsto q; it already suffices that \tau vanish on P_R and on \sigma_2 P_R. Since y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2 \neq 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), no word-level one-sidedness holds.

Where the weak vertex comes from. The definition of W rests on two inputs that are chosen, not derived.

  1. The one-sided requirement. W is required to act as \sigma^{-1} on one eigenline of \sigma and as \sigma on the other. This is an ansatz.
  2. The side. The eigenline on which W acts as \sigma^{-1} is the left line, by the definition of P_L above.

Given the two inputs, W is unique: an element x with x P_+ = a P_+ and x P_- = b P_- equals a P_+ + b P_-. With J = P_+ - P_- and |q| > 1, the two one-sided elements are

\sigma^{-1} P_+ + \sigma P_- \;=\; q^{-1} J, \qquad \sigma P_+ + \sigma^{-1} P_- \;=\; q\, J .

So W = q^{-1}J, and the element with the opposite side, qJ, differs from it only by the scalar q^2. The Proposition above follows from the inputs and is, in this sense, close to a restatement of them.

What this does not say. It does not identify W with the physical weak coupling.
prf:weak-vertex-left-projector:
Proof Proof of the weak vertex insertion identity. Since P_L + P_R = 1, every element x satisfies x = x P_L + x P_R. By definition W P_L = \sigma^{-1} P_L and W P_R = \sigma P_R. Hence

W - \sigma \;=\; (\sigma^{-1} - \sigma)\, P_L \;=\; -(q - q^{-1})\, P_L ,

using \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h, which follows from the Hecke relation. For consequence 1, use P_L P_R = 0 and P_L^2 = P_L. For consequence 2, write x = a + b\,\sigma. If x P_R = 0, then x = x P_L = (a + b\mu)\, P_L, where \mu is the eigenvalue of \sigma on the left line. The converse is P_L P_R = 0. For consequence 3, expand t\,\sigma - t^{-1}\sigma^{-1} with \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h. This gives (t - t^{-1})(\sigma + t^{-1}), which equals (t - t^{-1})(t + t^{-1}) times the projector onto the eigenvalue-t line, and that line is P_L by the choice of t.

The knot-level value is an exact symbolic computation over the three Wedderburn blocks of H_3(q), with the z = q^3/(q^2+1) Markov weights y_{(3)} = (q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)} = q^2/(q^2+1)^2, and y_{(1^3)} = 0. The same computation reproduces \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl((\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5\bigr) = q^2(q^{12}+q^8-1)/(q^2+1)^2.

For the trace characterisation, let \sigma_1 and \sigma_2 act on the two-dimensional block by explicit matrices that satisfy the Hecke and braid relations. Then \tau(P_R) = y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} and \tau(\sigma_2 P_R) = y_{(2,1)}\,q^3/(q^2+1) - y_{(1^3)}\,q^{-1}. If both vanish, then y_{(2,1)}(q^4+q^2+1) = 0, so y_{(2,1)} = y_{(1^3)} = 0 when [3]_q \neq 0. Conversely, P_R is zero on the trivial block, so the remaining term y_{(3)}\chi_{(3)}(x P_R) vanishes for every x. \square
prop:torus-knot-genus-four-unique:
Proposition Genus-4 torus knots: \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\} are the only solutions. Let g \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}. Consider torus knots T_{m,n} with 2 \leq m \leq n and \gcd(m, n) = 1. The genus is g(T_{m,n}) = (m-1)(n-1)/2 (torus knot generators). At g = 4, the equation (m-1)(n-1) = 8 has exactly two positive integer solutions with m \leq n and \gcd(m, n) = 1:

Solution (m, n) crossing number c = m(n-1) \gcd(m, n)
(m{-}1,\, n{-}1) = (1,\, 8) (2,\, 9) 9 1 (yes)
(m{-}1,\, n{-}1) = (2,\, 4) (3,\, 5) 10 1 (yes)
prf:torus-knot-genus-four-unique: Proof Proof of torus knot genus four unique. The Diophantine equation (m{-}1)(n{-}1) = 8 with 1 \leq m{-}1 \leq n{-}1 admits only the factorisations 8 = 1 \cdot 8 and 8 = 2 \cdot 4. The remaining 4 \cdot 2 and 8 \cdot 1 violate m \leq n or recover the listed solutions by the symmetry T_{m,n} \cong T_{n,m}. Coprimality \gcd(m,n) = 1 holds in both cases, so \{T_{2,9},\, T_{3,5}\} is the complete list of genus-4 torus knots up to mirror symmetry. \square
prop:force-carrier-bring-uniqueness: Proposition (T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}) is the unique pair of genus-4 torus knots. Bring's surface \Sigma_4 has genus 4. A torus knot K embeds as a saturating generator of the symplectic homology H_1(\Sigma_4, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}^{2 g} = \mathbb{Z}^8 only if g(K) = g(\Sigma_4) = 4. By the genus-4 classification, the force-carrier sector of any QOU built on \Sigma_4 is exactly \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\}.
prf:force-carrier-bring-uniqueness:
Proof Proof of force carrier bring uniqueness. The saturation condition selects torus knots whose Seifert genus matches the ambient surface's geometric genus. By the genus-4 uniqueness proposition, the only such torus knots are T_{2,9} (crossing number 9) and T_{3,5} (crossing number 10). \square

Corollary (categorical complexity of the force-carrier sector). Working over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q - q^{-1})^{-1}], the categorical q-dimensions assigned to the two force-carrier objects are \dim_q T_{2,9} = [9]_q and \dim_q T_{3,5} = [10]_q (the q-deformed crossing numbers). The total complexity of the force-carrier sector is

  \dim_q\bigl(T_{2,9}\bigr)
  \cdot
  \dim_q\bigl(T_{3,5}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  [9]_q \cdot [10]_q \,\in\, R.
rem:force-carrier-bring-uniqueness-novel: Remark Mathematical novelty of the genus-saturation force-carrier derivation. The Diophantine constraint (m-1)(n-1)=2g enforces genus-saturation on the symplectic homology of Bring's surface. This algebraic geometry condition determines the force-carrier pair (knots with 9 and 10 crossings). It eliminates the need for auxiliary symmetry assumptions.
prose:intro-em-completeness-gauge-coupli:
Because the photon spectrum saturates the two-strand color-neutral subspace of the exceptional divisor, the electromagnetic gauge coupling \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} is not an independent free parameter; it is determined by the spectral measure of the two-strand Hecke algebra.

This section proves the gauge-coupling uniqueness theorem from two-strand spectral completeness over a commutative ring R, derives the projection formula for \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}^{-1}(q) in terms of the basic quantum integer product q[9]_q[10]_q corrected by the Chern–Simons Gram-determinant ratio \delta_{\mathrm{CS}} and the spectral curvature \kappa, and shows how the infrared zero-mode on Bring's surface governs the fixed-point iteration toward the fine-structure constant.
rem:force-carrier-spectral-interpretatio:
Remark Force-carrier sector has no degrees of freedom. Three independent results force the denominator [9]_q \cdot [10]_q:

  1. The existence axiom for the quantum observable universe embeds the brane into a genus-4 modular curve.
  2. The genus-4 Diophantine classification exhausts torus knots of that genus by the pair \{T_{2,9}, T_{3,5}\}.
  3. The categorical q-dimension assignment to torus simples is a fixed datum of \mathbf{Rep}_q(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)).

The denominator of the fine structure constant is therefore a topological invariant of the Bring fibration.

Strong and weak labelling. The lower crossing number dominates gauge boson exchange. The assignment pairs T_{2,9} to the strong force and T_{3,5} to the weak force. This labelling does not affect the product [9]_q \cdot [10]_q. It identifies which torus knot mediates which sector.
cor:gauge-coupling-uniqueness: Corollary Uniqueness of the scalar gauge coupling on A \otimes A. Any R-linear, braid-invariant, scalar coupling A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1} is a multiple of \mathrm{tr}_\tau(e_-) \cdot e_-. Up to the global normalisation \lambda \in R, exactly one non-trivial scalar coupling exists on the two-strand sector of \mathbf{C}.
prf:gauge-coupling-uniqueness: Proof Proof of gauge coupling uniqueness. A scalar coupling factors through projection onto a singlet summand of A \otimes A. The completeness theorem provides exactly one such summand (V_- \cong \mathbf{1}, of R-rank one), and the projection onto it is e_-. Any R-linear, braid-invariant \phi \colon E \to R vanishing on V_+ therefore equals \lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_\tau(e_-) on e_-, with \lambda = \phi(e_-)/\mathrm{tr}_\tau(e_-) \in R. \square
rem:gauge-coupling-uniqueness-novelty: Remark Mathematical novelty of the scalar gauge-coupling uniqueness constraint. Spectral completeness constrains the gauge sector. It bounds possible gauge couplings strictly by algebraic singlets.
prop:em-coupling-projection:
Proposition Electromagnetic coupling from the antisymmetric braiding and force-carrier crossings. Setup. The categorical structure is defined over the commutative ring

  R \;=\; \mathbb{Z}\bigl[q^{\pm 1/2},\, (q - q^{-1})^{-1}\bigr].

Every quantity below lives in R and survives any ring map \iota \colon R \to k to a target commutative ring k.

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe over R with aether parameter q and force-carrier generators T_{2,9} (crossing number c_s = 9) and T_{3,5} (crossing number c_w = 10). The electromagnetic fine structure constant is the \tau-trace of the singlet idempotent e_- normalised by the force-carrier categorical complexity:

  \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}(q)
  = 
  \frac{q^{-1}}{[c_s]_q \cdot [c_w]_q}
  = 
  \frac{q^{-1}}{[9]_q \cdot [10]_q}

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer.

A cleared-denominator relation avoids division outside the integral Laurent subring \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \subset R:

  [9]_q \cdot [10]_q \cdot \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} \;=\; q^{-1}.
